Is it possible to destroy a planet Death Star style?
My guess would be super heating the core. But I don't think we can do that right now.
I'm sure, theorhetically, but definitely not in our lifetimes.
I would imagine it's theoretically possible, but we aren't anywhere close with current technology.

Like others have mentioned, its just matter of getting enough energy in the right place.

Large objects are held together by gravity. Gravity is a weak force, you overcome gravity every time you pick something up. These smaller things, such as walking, or explosions rely on electromagnetic interactions. Now, if its easy to beat gravity just with your arm, why can't you just get an explosion that should destroy a planet like a cracker in a pumpkin?

The issue is scale. These fundamental forces act differently at different length scales. Gravity is weak, but it stays weak over a huge scale. Electromagnetic forces are strong but fall off quickly.

As for validity of your original question, It is best to look at stars. The bigger the star, the more energy it produces, after all they are basically a continuous nuclear explosion on a huge scale. The energy trying to blow the star apart is counteracted by the gravity of all the matter in that star. When a star dies one of two things happen. If it is smaller, the fuel burns out and gravity wins, or it is big, it burns with enough energy that at a point there is not enough gravity to hold back the explosion and boom, star goes away, death star style.

So basically it takes the entire energy of a large star to overcome gravity like that. The death star or even the earth would not contain enough fissile material to create energy like that. There is no feasible way to make the planet go poof.

Of course, we could get an explosion that would break the planet up into little chunks, but they would eventually all conglomerate back into a sphere, gravity is hard to beat.
